subject: SIEM & trace export for NorthStar private deployment
messages:
From: Julie Hart <julie.hart@northstarbank.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: northstar-security@northstarbank.com
Date: 2028-10-05T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial SIEM / trace export questions for private deployment

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting the security review for the Redwood private deployment in our VPC and have a few specific questions about observability exports before we lock networking and procurement. Attached is our SIEM questionnaire (nsb_siem_questionnaire.pdf). High level asks:

- What egress patterns do you support from a private deployment that does not allow unrestricted internet egress?
- Can Redwood push logs to our S3 bucket over a VPC endpoint, or do you require a managed forwarder?
- What transport options are supported for Splunk ingestion (HEC vs syslog vs forwarder) and do any require outbound ports to vendor IPs?
- Trace forwarding: do you support sampling rate configuration, and what metadata do you preserve (trace ids, parent ids, X-Request-Id mapping)?
- Evidence & chain of custody: how do you package audit logs for compliance requests and what controls exist around access?

We also need a topology diagram with specific CIDR/IP ranges you expect to talk to. Can you provide a minimal firewall rule set we can give our networking team?

Julie
Security Programs
NorthStar Bank

Attachment: nsb_siem_questionnaire.pdf

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Hart <julie.hart@northstarbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-05T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SIEM / trace export questions for private deployment

Hi Julie,

Appreciate the detail and the questionnaire — we'll work through it. Quick responses and a proposed next step:

- Egress patterns: Redwood private supports three common models: 1) push to customer-owned S3 via VPC gateway endpoint, 2) push to an in-VPC forwarder (Splunk universal forwarder or our lightweight forwarder) over MTLS, 3) proxy to a managed collector in a peered account. All models can be configured with no general internet egress.
- Splunk ingestion: we support HEC over HTTPS (recommended), syslog over TLS, and universal forwarder. HEC requires outbound HTTPS to the HEC endpoint; with a customer-managed HEC in their VPC there is no public egress.
- Traces: sampling is configurable per service; we preserve trace id, span id, parent id, and include an internal redwood_request_id to map tokens to traces.
- Evidence: we can bundle audit logs with MD5 checksums and provide timebound download links via a customer-managed S3 location.

Attached: redwood_vpc_obsv_options.pdf with a short topology diagram and minimal firewall rules (two IP ranges: 52.34.128.0/20 for control plane and your S3 endpoints or forwarder IPs).

Let's schedule a 30m technical handoff with your networking and security leads. Kimberly and Karthik — can you join tomorrow morning PT?

Thanks,
Logan
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_vpc_obsv_options.pdf

Julie,

A few compliance items to flag up front so we can avoid surprises during legal/infosec signoff:

- Key management: for audit artifacts and any exported PII, we require customer-managed KMS for S3 encryption or an approved HSM key; we'll document KMS ARNs and key rotation cadence.
- Access controls: we will restrict Redwood operational access to the minimum set of engineer identities and provide audit logs for any operator actions.
- Evidence packaging: standard practice is to deliver a signed evidence bundle and an audit manifest. If NorthStar requires additional notarization/signed receipt, we can scope that as a one-time compliance deliverable.

Please include the SOC2 report request in the same thread and we'll route that to our compliance team.

Kimberly
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Julie Hart <julie.hart@northstarbank.com>
Date: 2028-10-06T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SIEM / trace export questions for private deployment

Hi all,

Technical notes for the network team (minimal rule set and configs):

- Ports & protocols: outbound TCP 443 for HEC over HTTPS; outbound TCP 6514 for syslog over TLS if using a remote collector; persistent TCP connections for our forwarder to the collector on configurable port.
- IPs: we can publish static egress IP ranges for the control plane; for dedicated private deployments we can pin to a customer-provided NAT IP or use VPC endpoints so no public egress is necessary.
- MTLS: forwarder model uses mutual TLS with client certs rotated every 90 days. We'll provide cert signing requests and a small cert-rotation tool.
- Trace semantics: we inject redwood_request_id and propagate incoming trace headers (traceparent and tracetools). Sampling is configured at service-level via the runtime; default is 1% for production with configurable per-route overrides.
- Quotas & SLOs: log delivery SLOs depend on path — VPC-to-S3 pushes are near-batch (1-5 min), HEC over HTTPS is near-real-time (under 10s median), forwarder TCP is streaming. We'll include recommended sampling and batching knobs to keep latency within your SIEM retention windows.

Attached: redwood_trace_hook_spec.md (lightweight spec for header mappings and sampling controls).

Karthik
Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_trace_hook_spec.md
